title: Chicago bands, jobs and recordings with Sims; Chicago versus New York
summary: He recalls jobs like Riverview, copying Dutrey and Oliver note for note, recording on Paramount, and argues Chicago led New York then.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I talked to him the other day.

He had a studio right there at 36th Estate you know. He had the band in Milwaukee, the Wisconsin roof, before Sims had it. He comes or he leaves there and goes to Savoy. That's when Sims goes on in there and when Sims is about a year or so I go in there with Sims. But he had a good band, he had a good band, he had good Harmon's Bremen. He had Riverview. He and Cook, those fellas, they had some of the best jobs to be had. McGuire's down on Clark Street. I follow Roy and Dutray and him all around. And I get into places like McGuire's and all those places. See? I get into those places. But I follow Dutray. It was an honor to carry them fellas' horns. I carried the horns for them. And I don't regret it. I ever met the Lil' Whitties was great. And I see them meet them fellas and we had a little band, we copied right behind Joy of them, note for note. Every time they made a record, note for note, note for note. But he was playing this Snaggit, that Snaggit and all that stuff, note for note. And we recorded. I have a record here now I think of Buddy Helms' band. One side is Joff and the other is Buddy Helms. On the Paramount. We recorded. We recorded the Tin Roof Band. Did you ever have any record? Yeah, I have that record. And then I had a little band of my own with all this stuff. Did you ever hear that record? I found the- Yeah. I recorded my own little band of Shirley Clay. That's nice. Shirley Clay, you hear? Yeah. That was nice. Later on they played with Don Redmond, Shirley Clay, nice trumpet player. I mean they had a lot of good trumpet players from St. Louis and Kansas City. I mean all of them didn't come from New Orleans, see? But they were the pioneers, you see, and a lot of those boys went on that boat down there, they're sitting in this boat down there in New Orleans, and got a lot of stuff from them boys, that's possible. But I know like Bob Schaffner, Bob Schaffner's a good Dixieland, you've heard him over there, and Bob Schaffner and this boy had St. Louis all locked up, Charlie- Crep. Charlie Crep, yeah. He was great. He was great too. You see what I'm talking about? Yeah, sure. And they had musicians from out east that was good too. But Chicago was the king, New York at that time, the great Fletcher Henderson and the Duke of Henderson wasn't heard of. Wasn't heard of. They wasn't heard of. They wasn't heard of. When Joe Oliver had his band, that great band of his, they wasn't heard of. Fletcher later on, St. Louis and Tommy Ladner, that's another boy. That Tommy Ladner could play a whole lot of trumpet. He joined Fletcher later on. See what I'm talking about? He said for those fellas, Fletcher didn't have the band. Those fellas helped make the band that Fletcher laid on. Hawkins, I just heard a little bit about Hawkins. Then we had Stumpy Evans. You ever hear of Stumpy Evans?
